Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:55pm

By Joshua Boscaini

Thanks for sticking with us. We'll be back tomorrow for another day on the federal politics live blog.

You can look back at today's developments below, or download the ABC News app and subscribe to our range of news alerts for the latest updates.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:49pm

By Jack McKay

Labor stalwart and former foreign minister Gareth Evans has suggested it is not in Australia's national interest to remain in the AUKUS submarine pact.

Evans, who served in the Hawke and Keating governments, has appeared before a crowd-funded public inquiry that is probing the security agreement.

He told the inquiry the AUKUS project was "misconceived" from the start.

"The passage of time, since its announcement in 2021, assert only to make more compelling the conclusion that it is not in Australia's national interest to continue our commitment to it," he said.

"There are huge doubts about its deliverability, its cost to Australia manifestly outweighs its benefits, and its implementation will profoundly limit Australia's independent sovereign agency."

Evans said there was "zero certainty" about the timely delivery of the submarines promised under the agreement.

"Every piece of evidence now available on the public record reinforces scepticism as to whether any of them will be delivered on time, or indeed at all," he said.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:43pm

By Joshua Boscaini

State and territory disability ministers have accused the Albanese government of pushing on with NDIS changes that do not align with previous agreements, warning the pace of the overhaul risks the safety of people with disability.

In a stinging joint submission to the Labor-led Senate inquiry examining the bill, state ministers said the proposal for change went "beyond and contrasted with" the recommendations of previous reviews and was "inconsistent with commitments by all governments" made at national cabinet in January.

The Senate inquiry has spent the last three days hearing concerns from across the disability sector and received more than 4,000 public submissions in just over a fortnight.

Under the proposed overhaul, the federal government expects about 300,000 people to be either kicked off or prevented from accessing the now-$50 billion scheme, with many to be serviced by yet-to-be-built supports to be run by the states.

Read the full story from the Specialist Reporting Team's Evan Young and Mary Lloyd, with national disability affairs reporter Nas Campanella.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:40pm

By Joshua Boscaini

Pauline Hanson has backed the One Nation WA senator under the microscope for his links to a family company that receives work from a Commonwealth agency.

Some media outlets are reporting that Tyron Whitten could be in breach of section 44 of the constitution because his family company reportedly has links to Snowy Hydro.

"We've got legal advice on it and he's very strong. There's no section 44 whatsoever," Hanson says.

Asked if she will release the legal advice, Hanson wouldn't say.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:33pm

By Joshua Boscaini

Pauline Hanson says the current GST carve-up is not fair, but she wouldn't support a change in the distribution.

Changes to GST distribution made by the Morrison government in 2018 mean WA keeps at least 75 cents for every dollar of GST revenue.

Speaking from Perth, the One Nation leader said she didn't believe the settings were fair, but she wouldn't advocate for WA's share to be "lost at all".

"I think the other states need to start utilising their resources to create productivity in their own states. They've been slack to do it, and they're relying on other states to prop them up all the time," Hanson says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:24pm

By Joshua Boscaini

One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson is holding a short press conference after speaking at a business breakfast in Perth this morning.

This morning the prime minister questioned whether One Nation had actually received more than $1.8 million through its fundraising drive.

Hanson says the fundraising is "very legitimate" and that the party will get an independent auditor to go through the donations.

"Everyone who donates should get a receipt sent back to them. So very legitimate. Why would I put it all out?" Hanson says.

She's taken a jab at the prime minister and Labor, questioning how much the party has raised through its own fundraising drive.

"He can't even believe it himself. I heard on the grapevine he's only received about $20,000 for the Labor Party, so he can't imagine One Nation getting the support that we have," she says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 1:11pm

By Keane Bourke

The media has been booted from a business breakfast One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson was speaking at this morning.

Often when politicians attend events with representative groups like this, the media is given free access because there's a public interest in reporting what they say.

Otherwise, they are denied access altogether when the event is considered private. It's unusual for journalists to be asked to pay for access.

But today the Swan Chamber of Commerce, hosting the One Nation leader at the event on Perth's north-eastern fringes, said journalists would have to pay $60 per person to gain entry.

That's despite One Nation allowing two media outlets to film the event without having to pay.

Hanson snuck into the event without taking any questions from the waiting press pack.

The party's WA leader, Rod Caddies, did stop, though, and said it was up to the chamber how it wanted to handle the event.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 12:28pm

By Nicholas McElroy

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has ruled out an MP's suggestion the Coalition should carve up the seats it contests with One Nation at the next federal election.

It comes as Pauline Hanson's party says its "Fire the Liar" fundraiser has brought in $1.6 million in one day.

Liberal frontbencher Tony Pasin has told The Australian newspaper the party could work "hand in glove" with One Nation to target seats each party had a chance of winning from Labor.

Pasin's proposal comes amid One Nation's rapid fundraising effort and multiple polls finding that voters were more likely to vote for One Nation than any other party.

Read the full story from political reporter Nicholas McElroy in the link below.

Key Event

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 11:25am

By Joshua Boscaini

One of Pauline Hanson's closest advisers says he "stole" the slogan for One Nation's fundraising campaign from Sky News host Peta Credlin.

The right-wing party says it has received more than $1.8 million in donations, and has revised up its fundraising goal to $2 million.

Ashby says 28,000 people have made a contribution to the campaign and that the party is willing to get the donation website independently audited by a forensics team to verify the donations are real.

Asked who came up with the line "fire the liar", Ashby says he took it from Credlin.

"You wouldn't believe it, but I was talking to Peta Credlin and I was watching her show and I stole it off her. Nothing quite like a borrowed line right then," Ashby says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 11:07am

By Tom Crowley

Treasurer Jim Chalmers has just made a speech at Labor's National Policy Forum, telling the party faithful the government's budget shows it has the answers to the rise of populism and division.

He says politics is split between "three right-wing parties who see economic and social division and divisive politics around the world and want to replicate that here … and a Labor government determined to actually address it."

"The irony of their position is they want to change the government in order to leave everything as it is, a truly absurd proposition," he says, adding that the controversy about the budget's tax changes has been driven "by the biggest beneficiaries … not the biggest victims of the broken status quo".

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 11:03am

By Joshua Boscaini

The prime minister has criticised One Nation and the Nationals for voting against legislation to implement a gun buyback scheme.

Asked if he was prepared to run a national gun buyback scheme if the states and territories did not get onboard with it, the PM encouraged jurisdictions to work with the Commonwealth.

But Anthony Albanese has veered into territory unrelated to gun buybacks and has criticised "dysfunction" in the Coalition.

"It's very clear that what it will be about is Labor, as the only mainstream party that is concerned with everyday Australians, are making a difference, that's prepared to govern across the suite of policy issues to make a difference for people's lives," he says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 11:00am

By Joshua Boscaini

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has defended the government's attempts to stop the spread of illicit tobacco in Australia.

Albanese says the government has ramped up funding for organisations working with the Australian Border Force and state and federal police.

"We are taking action against the illicit tobacco trade. We'll continue to do so," Albanese says.

"We're taking action, whether it be the enforcement of supplies [or] the shutting down of shops that are selling illicit tobacco."

Key Event

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 10:54am

By Joshua Boscaini

The PM has left the door open to extending the fuel excise cut in the wake of the latest flare-up in fighting in the Middle East.

Anthony Albanese says the government is "deeply concerned" about the escalating crisis and calls for de-escalation.

The prime minister says the federal government will continue to examine the price of fuel in the coming weeks.

"We'll continue to monitor those issues which are there at the moment. The price of fuel has decreased substantially from where it was," Albanese says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 10:50am

By Joshua Boscaini

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has stepped up for a press conference in Sydney to announce funding for arthritis research.

He's announced $100 million for a new arthritis and musculoskeletal conditions research mission in Sydney.

The prime minister been asked about Pauline Hanson's pledge to target Labor seats, including those of a high-profile minister, at the next election.

Albanese says Labor will continue to campaign against "the three right-wing parties".

He says  Tony Pasin's reported proposal to carve up seats at the next election between the Liberals and One Nation is "extraordinary".

"That says it all about the way that the once-mainstream Liberal Party has become just a fringe party, almost giving up two years before an election is held," Albanese says.

"We're very confident that we'll continue to put forward comprehensive policy plans."

Albanese has questioned whether One Nation has really received $1.8 million in donations during its fundraising drive.

Key Event

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 10:00am

By Joshua Boscaini

Last night, One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson singled out Tony Burke's seat as a target for her party during the next election campaign.

The home affairs minister says Hanson "hates" his part of Western Sydney.

"People shouldn't pretend to be patriotic if they hate modern Australia. I love Australia, and I love Australia for who we are. Not for some fake idea of the nation that we've never been," Burke says.

"As a message to people who want to demean their fellow Australians, we're a better country than that."

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 9:56am

By Joshua Boscaini

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has stepped up for a press conference following his speech, and he's been asked how much taxpayers will have to fork out to compensate the NZYQ cohort.

There are warnings a High Court ruling allowing a man to sue for false imprisonment over his indefinite immigration detention will lead to more claims running into the tens of millions of dollars.

The home affairs minister says the government is still working through the decision that came down yesterday.

"The courts have not yet made any orders with respect to compensation, but an argument that the Commonwealth put was rejected," Burke says.

"Let me say this as a matter of principle, though. If your visa is cancelled, you should leave Australia and each of the individuals we're talking about are individuals who had their visas cancelled and did not leave Australia."

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 9:46am

By Joshua Boscaini

Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke says artificial intelligence makes it possible to fake voices and direct people to open vulnerabilities in their systems, thinking they're following the orders of their bosses.

The home affairs minister has equated the practice to email and text message phishing, but says "voice phishing" is a lot more sophisticated.

"We need to remember these systems are getting more sophisticated and we should not simply view the cyber-attack as being data sets that flow through, and that try to get through with false passwords or trying to undo encryption," Burke says.

"We need to recognise the weakest link may well be the people who are not the bad employee, but actually not the trusted insider who behaves the wrong way, but somebody who thinks they are doing what they are told."

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 9:38am

By Joshua Boscaini

Horizon 2 involves equipping people with the skills to ward off cyber threats to businesses and infrastructure, the home affairs minister says.

Tony Burke says the three main areas Horizon 2 will look at are vulnerabilities related to infrastructure, devices and people.

The home affairs minister says 60 per cent of vulnerabilities related to cyber threats are human error.

He says Australia also needs to classify and secure Australia's subsea cables and secure data sets of national significance.

"We cannot continue to have a situation where there is just a mixture between infrastructure, between the communications portfolio, between home affairs with a clear interest from defence as well without starting to streamline farm or effectively how we deal with the regulation, and protection of our subsea cables," Burke says.

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 9:27am

By Joshua Boscaini

Tony Burke has stepped up for a speech to launch Horizon 2 of the Cyber Security Strategy ahead of a meeting of the Executive Cyber Council.

The home affairs minister says the average cost of cybercrime in the past 12 months has increased by 50 per cent.

Burke says Australia won't be able to effectively deal with cybersecurity threats without everyone working together.

"Cybersecurity is a team sport and so effectively, while competition law quite properly wants to keep people apart, unless we can get people to the same table, we cannot effectively deal with this," Burke says.

"That is an essential and absolutely essential aspect of being able to deal with cyber security."

Thu 11 Jun 2026 at 9:08am

By Joshua Boscaini

In calmer times, a World Cup fixture might have offered Anthony Albanese a useful piece of informal diplomacy. These are not calmer times.

Barring an unlikely last-minute invitation from Donald Trump, the prime minister won't be zipping across the Pacific next week to cheer on the Socceroos against the United States.

The sports-loving prime minister had publicly mused about a potential trip to Seattle. The idea was to catch up with the president in a less formal setting. It might have helped smooth over Trump's criticism of Australia for not offering more help in the war with Iran.

But alas, no invitation has come. Nor is it clear whether Trump will even be there.
